title: Scale-aware discovery density and authored hierarchy

scope.subject: Make the existing Places/Navigator presentation density scale-aware across Galaxy and System while preserving full Search/filter long-tail access and authored personal hierarchy

research_summary: Agent 07 requires discovery density to change with scale and generated/catalog filler not to overwhelm authored content. Personal Universe already has one continuous 0..5 scale coordinate, canonical grouped Places sections, React-derived presentation and YEIS/native navigation. Reuse those authorities: pass the current continuous scale coordinate into Navigator, apply deterministic per-section presentation budgets only to the default empty-query All view, spotlight only high-importance/featured Personal Signals so lower-priority authored items can remain visible under their semantic Projects/Research/etc groups, and leave Search plus explicit Personal/Important/Nearby/Recent filters uncapped by the default density profile. This is DOM/presentation budgeting, not renderer LOD or a second content index.

sources.finding: Cosmos demonstrates scale-regime and LOD concepts for large browser universes, but replacing Personal Universe discovery/rendering would be disproportionate; reuse the existing continuous scale coordinate as a presentation-density signal.
React memoized derived presentation is sufficient for deterministic section budgets without changing the canonical destination graph or adding persistent state.
Existing Playwright acceptance can compare Galaxy/System visible row budgets and verify Search/filter paths still expose the long tail.

search_ladder.conclusion: Retain Personal Universe on pinned YEIS and borrow only the scale-regime/LOD principle; do not replace the product with another universe engine.
Use existing React derived presentation and the existing continuous scale value; no new reactive or virtualization framework is required at current volume.
Keep YEIS navigation/catalog resolution intact and budget only the product Places rows rendered by the existing Navigator.
Reuse hosted Playwright to validate scale-aware DOM density and long-tail accessibility through real product surfaces.

candidates.name: Continuous-scale-derived Places presentation budgets
candidates.source: Existing continuous 0..5 scale plus canonical Places sections
candidates.license: project product layer over pinned MIT YEIS
candidates.reason: Changes only visible default Places density while keeping one canonical graph, full Search/filter access, navigation identity and renderer ownership.

candidates.name: React memoized section budgeting
candidates.reason: Deterministically derives a small visible set from already-loaded sections and avoids extra index/database/state machinery.

candidates.name: Third-party list virtualization for Navigator
candidates.reason: Default Places should not render hundreds of rows in the first place; bounded semantic budgets solve product comprehension and DOM size at lower integration cost.

candidates.name: Renderer-owned discovery LOD/state
candidates.reason: Would violate Agent 07 coordination boundaries by moving discovery policy into renderer/camera ownership and would duplicate the continuous scale coordinator.

candidates.name: Existing hosted Playwright density acceptance
candidates.reason: Can prove Galaxy/System density differences and long-tail Search access without a separate performance or discovery harness.

coverage_matrix.capability: Galaxy default Places emphasizes major authored/system-level signals with bounded DOM rows
coverage_matrix.decision: Apply low Galaxy limits per semantic section and only spotlight featured/high-importance Personal Signals in the catch-all Personal group.

coverage_matrix.capability: System scale exposes more body/local destinations without changing canonical identity
coverage_matrix.decision: Interpolate section limits from Galaxy to System using the existing continuous scale coordinate, with a larger body budget at System.

coverage_matrix.capability: Search and explicit filters retain long-tail discoverability
coverage_matrix.decision: Apply scale budgets only to empty-query All Places; explicit filters and Search operate on the full canonical candidate set.

coverage_matrix.capability: Generated/catalog content does not overwhelm authored personal hierarchy
coverage_matrix.decision: Reserve authored spotlight capacity and deterministic per-category quotas before generic catalog rows.

decision.rationale: Use the product's existing continuous scale coordinate solely as a deterministic presentation-density input. Canonical graph, Search, explicit filters, navigation state and renderer/camera ownership remain unchanged.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: Virtualization optimizes an oversized list but does not solve the product problem of presenting too much generic content by default.
Renderer-side policy would couple content discovery to another agent's domain and duplicate scale/navigation authority.

decision.fallback: If future catalogs become too large even after semantic quotas, virtualize only the already-ranked visible-result surface; never move canonical identity or ranking ownership into the renderer.
